answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with an age-graded fee signal: every fresh identity pays a high transaction fee that decays as it accumulates verified work, so a farm running thousands of newborn accounts bleeds money on each one while honest agents quickly earn the low-fee tier. The network takes the pulse of each identity by sampling its recent transactions; a genuine history forms a pearl of earned trust that cannot be bought or faked in bulk, because fees are charged per identity, not per owner.
